```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(here)
library(knitr)

theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical"))

gpkg_file <- here::here("outputs", "gis", "MI_OPW_tidal_analysis_v2.gpkg")

if (!file.exists(gpkg_file)) {
  stop(paste0("GeoPackage not found at: ", gpkg_file, "\nRun the GIS export script first."))
}
```

# Introduction

This notebook demonstrates the GIS layers produced from the MI/OPW tidal analysis.

The GeoPackage contains station locations, station-level tidal-feature estimates, and separate spatio-temporal prediction layers for HAT, MHWS, MHWN, MSL, MLWN, MLWS and LAT.

The prediction layers contain posterior mean estimates, posterior standard deviations and 95% credible intervals for every prediction location and year.

# GeoPackage contents

```{r layers}
gpkg_layers <- st_layers(gpkg_file)
gpkg_layers
```


# Station locations

The `stations` layer contains one point for each tide-gauge station included in the analysis. It does not contain any tidal feature estimates, simply the location of tide-gauge stations. 

```{r read-stations}
stations <- st_read(gpkg_file, layer = "stations", quiet = TRUE)

stations
```



## Station map

Plotting the station points alone produces the following map.

```{r station-map, fig.width=5, fig.height=7}
stations |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(size = 2) +
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(2157), xlim = c(350000, 800000), ylim = c(450000, 1050000), expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  labs(title = "Tide-gauge stations", x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)")
```

Superimposing the points onto a shapefile of Ireland produces the following map.
```{r, fig.width=5, fig.height=7}
## Ireland shapefile
ireland <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", country = "Ireland", returnclass = "sf")

## Plot stations over Ireland
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = ireland, fill = "grey95", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_sf(data = stations, size = 2) +
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(2157), xlim = c(350000, 800000), ylim = c(450000, 1050000), expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +  labs(title = "Tide-gauge stations", x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "aliceblue", colour = NA))
```

# Station-level tidal features

The `tidal_features` layer contains the tidal characteristics calculated at the tide-gauge stations using the rolling-window harmonic analysis.

Each row represents one station and one midpoint year. HAT, MHWS, MHWN, MSL, MLWN, MLWS and LAT are stored as separate fields.

```{r read-tidal-features}
tidal_features <- st_read(gpkg_file, layer = "tidal_features", quiet = TRUE)

tidal_features |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  arrange(StationID, Year) |>
  slice_head(n = 20) |>
  kable(digits = 3)
```

## Available years

Below we check the range of the temporal data provided in the `tidal_features` layer.

```{r tidal-feature-years}
tidal_features |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarise(first_year = min(Year, na.rm = TRUE), last_year = max(Year, na.rm = TRUE), n_years = n_distinct(Year)) |>
  kable()
```

## Example station-level tidal-feature map

Below we choose the Mean High Water Springs tidal feature, along with the final year of the analysis, and we can plot this feature at each tide gauge station.

```{r tidal-feature-settings, fig.width=5, fig.height=7}
station_feature <- "MHWS"

station_year <- tidal_features |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(!is.na(.data[[station_feature]])) |>
  summarise(year = max(Year, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(year)

tidal_features |>
  filter(Year == station_year, !is.na(.data[[station_feature]])) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = .data[[station_feature]]), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(direction = -1) +
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(2157), xlim = c(350000, 800000), ylim = c(450000, 1050000), expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +  labs(title = paste(station_feature, "Station-Level Estimates:", station_year), x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)", colour = paste0(station_feature, " (m)"))
```

## Tidal features through time at one station

We can also extract and plot tidal features through time. Below we choose Adelphi Quay, and examine all tidal features associated with this station. 

```{r example-station-settings, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
example_station <- tidal_features |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(StationID, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  pull(StationID)


tidal_features |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(StationID == example_station) |>
  select(Year, HAT, MHWS, MHWN, MSL, MLWN, MLWS, LAT) |>
  pivot_longer(-Year, names_to = "Tidal_feature", values_to = "Value") |>
  filter(!is.na(Value)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = Value, colour = Tidal_feature)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = paste("Station-level tidal features:", example_station), x = "Year", y = "Tidal level (m)", colour = "Tidal feature")
```

# Spatio-temporal prediction layers

The GeoPackage contains a prediction layer for each tidal feature. The names of each layer are:

```{r prediction-layer-names}
prediction_layer_names <- paste0("pred_", c("HAT", "MHWS", "MHWN", "MSL", "MLWN", "MLWS", "LAT"))

prediction_layer_names
```

Each prediction layer contains:

- `year_idx`: model time index;
- `year_mid`: calendar year represented by that time index;
- `longitude` and `latitude`: prediction coordinates;
- `mean`: posterior mean tidal-level prediction;
- `sd`: posterior standard deviation;
- `q025`: lower bound of the 95% credible interval;
- `q975`: upper bound of the 95% credible interval;
- `geometry`: GIS point geometry.

Note: Each prediction layer is large, so in this notebook we read only the layer currently being used and remove it from memory afterwards. 

## HAT Predictions

In this section we read in the `pred_HAT` layer, examine it in tabular form and create maps to examine both the mean predicted HAT over the study area and the associated standard deviation.

```{r hat-read, fig.width=5, fig.height=7}
# Read in HAT prediction layer
pred_HAT <- st_read(gpkg_file, layer = "pred_HAT", quiet = TRUE)

# Examine its structure
pred_HAT |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  kable(digits = 3)

# Choose a year to create a map
hat_year <- max(pred_HAT$year_mid, na.rm = TRUE) # final year of predictions

# Create a map of predictions for the mean HAT
pred_HAT |>
  filter(year_mid == hat_year) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = mean), size = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(direction = -1) +
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(2157), xlim = c(350000, 800000), ylim = c(450000, 1050000), expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +  labs(title = paste("Predicted HAT:", hat_year), x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)", colour = "Mean (m)")

# Create a map of predictions for the HAT standard deviation
pred_HAT |>
  filter(year_mid == hat_year) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = sd), size = 0.8) +
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(2157), xlim = c(350000, 800000), ylim = c(450000, 1050000), expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +  scale_colour_viridis_c(direction = -1) +
  labs(title = paste("HAT Prediction Uncertainty:", hat_year), x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)", colour = "SD (m)")

# cleanup HAT layer
rm(pred_HAT)
```

## Comparing prediction layers

The following summary compares the range of posterior mean predictions and uncertainty across the seven prediction layers.

```{r prediction-summary}
prediction_summary <- map_dfr(prediction_layer_names, \(layer_name) {
    x <- st_read(gpkg_file, layer = layer_name, quiet = TRUE)

    out <- x |>
      st_drop_geometry() |>
      summarise(
        first_year = min(year_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
        last_year = max(year_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
        n_rows = n(),
        mean_min = min(mean, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean_max = max(mean, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd_median = median(sd, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd_max = max(sd, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
      mutate(tidal_feature = str_remove(layer_name, "^pred_"), .before = 1)

    rm(x)
    gc(verbose = FALSE)

    out
  }
)

prediction_summary |>
  kable(digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    col.names = c(
      "Tidal feature",
      "First year",
      "Last year",
      "Rows",
      "Minimum predicted mean",
      "Maximum predicted mean",
      "Median SD",
      "Maximum SD"))
```
